gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the 5 kWh-class batteries' cycle-life ratings on the same end-of-life basis: Anker rates the S5000's 10,000 cycles to a battery still holding more than 60% of its capacity, while BLUETTI rates the B300K at 6,000+ cycles to 80% and gives no retention figure for the B4810's 6,000 cycles. The headline cycle counts therefore can't be compared as printed.
standout_why: I compared four pages. StormWatts' 240 V solar-input comparison (cited, 2026-11-16) gives only the S5000's '10,000 cycles', in its sources list, and gives no cycle life for Jackery, EcoFlow or the F3800 Plus. It never says what capacity a rating is measured to. EnergySage (cited) gives one generic figure for LFP batteries ('3,000 charge cycles or more') and no per-product cycle life. StormWatts' bundle-vs-separately page (cited) has no cycle life at all. None of them lists both continuous and surge AC for all candidates: StormWatts gives no surge figure for the Jackery 5000 Plus, and none of them mentions that the RV5 accepts at most 50 V open-circuit from the panels. I couldn't read Lights On Labs, a cited page, because the fetch failed with a self-signed certificate error, so I can't rule it out.
decides: On its own this doesn't pick the kit. It does stop the S5000's '10,000 cycles' from looking like 1.7× BLUETTI's 6,000. The 10,000 runs down to 60% capacity, against BLUETTI's 80% for the B300K, which is a looser end point. Most important for the pick: on 2026-11-17 BLUETTI's own RV5 page showed the 5kWh RV Kit as 'Out of Stock'. The 'Kits we link' table says 'ships now', so recheck stock before naming the RV5 kit as the ships-now pick. If it is out of stock, every Apex 300 or Apex 200 + B300K kit we link is a late-January-2027 pre-order. Separately, the RV5's 50 V open-circuit limit on panel input means its 100 W panels must be wired in parallel. Any panels a shopper adds must fit that limit too.
